thread:
incident-bot: ALERT · Streaming p99 spike detected in eu-west1 (ingress proxy). p99 > 12s, p95 ~ 1.8s. paging on-call

sre-oncall: I'm on it. what are the affected routes?

maya: Observed most from /v1/streaming/generate and websocket clients. Lots of stalled chunks and tcp conn resets from the proxy.

kai: Dashboards show proxy write latency climbing and multiple backend worker retries. Client backpressure counters up ~3x baseline.

leo: Customer-facing SIGMETRICS: a few active customers reported long pauses in streaming responses (their UX shows spinner ~10-20s). No 5xx spike at backend mounting yet.

sam-cs: FYI @customer-success — customer support is getting DMs. Potential P1 if SLA-affecting.

incident-bot: RUNBOOK STEP: Check proxy keepalive + slow-client eviction flags.

ops-bot: Quick check: proxy pool cpu normal, but socket write queue depth high on edge-3. Config snapshot: `keepalive_idle=120s`, `evict_slow_clients=false`

maya: Recommending toggling `evict_slow_clients=true` for eu-west1 edge pool and reduce `keepalive_idle` to 30s to free stale sockets.

kai: Agree. Also reduce max_in_flight_per_conn to 1 for streaming routes to avoid head-of-line due to blocked consumers.

leo: Applying change to canary subset now (edge-3a). Will patch via infra-runbook: `gcloud compute instances update ... --restart` (small restart).

sre-oncall: Canary patch applied to edge-3a: evict=true, keepalive=30s, max_in_flight_per_conn=1. Monitoring.

incident-bot: NOTE · After change: p99 on canary dropped from 12.4s -> 2.1s in 4m. p95 unchanged.

maya: We should roll to rest of eu-west1 in controlled window. Will do 2 nodes at a time. Also add a temporary routing rule to send new traffic to eu-central if client's origin is flagged and socket age > 60s.

kai: Also enabling fallback routing to low-latency model variant for streaming (`redwood/compact-v1`) to reduce token runtime while we stabilize.

sam-cs: Customers asked for ETA. Suggest: "mitigating, expect partial relief in ~10-20m, full roll ~40m".

leo: Rolling to edge-3b/3c now. Pacing 2 nodes every 90s.

ops-bot: Command used:
```
infractl edge update --region eu-west1 --pool edge-3 --set evict_slow_clients=true,keepalive_idle=30,max_in_flight_per_conn=1 --batch 2
```

sre-oncall: Logs: seeing many long-lived client connections with zero bytes read for >30s preceded by bursty writes then stall. Suspect a subset of WebSocket clients that don't ACK.

maya: We're enabling a short-term proxy metric alert to paging if write queue depth > 500 for >3m.

kai: On the backend side, adding a guard to stop excessive backpressure propagation: if socket write queue > 1000, worker will drop to buffered-only mode and return a streaming keepalive token every 2s to prevent client timeouts. Patch queued and hotpatching one worker pool in canary.

incident-bot: CUSTOMER IMPACT: Medium — degraded streaming experience for some customers in eu-west1. No data loss reported, but UX interruption.

sam-cs: Notifying top affected customers with a brief note.

leo: Roll complete across eu-west1. Post-roll telemetry: p99 down to 1.9s cluster-wide, error rates stable. Monitoring for recurrence.

sre-oncall: Will keep on-call for 60m watch. Handing to morning SRE: @maya please pick up status in 30m?

maya: Acknowledged. I'll monitor logs, traces, and coordinate with CS.

kai: Follow-ups: 1) add automated slow-client eviction in proxy by default, 2) add a streaming handshake health-check to detect half-open clients, 3) run a customer traffic replay to validate keepalive changes.

sam-cs: Recording incident notes for outreach. Flagging 2 customers for postmortem comms.

ops-bot: Saved runbook snapshot: `runbook/streaming/evict-keepalive-v1` -> tag v2026-03-17-evict

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS · Mitigated -> watch. Assign: investigation -> SRE team. Priority: P2 (reclassified from potential P1 after mitigation).

sre-oncall: Handoff done. Last checks: traces show no new long-tail goroutine stalls, client eviction logs present. If recurrence, escalate back to P1.

maya: Closing handoff. I'll collate traces + timeline into the incident doc and create follow-up tickets for the Kai items.

leo: Thanks team. :thumbsup:
